top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a new classification of electronic matter: Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal-invariant, spin-orbit-coupled insulators split into Z2 classes with protected helical edge states, and Molenkamp's HgTe quantum-well conductance measurement made it an observed phase. It is mature (two decades of transport, ARPES and STM confirmation), distinct from the 2016 prize (time-reversal symmetry preserved, no applied field), and the 2D-limited citation keeps the contested 3D and HgTe-proposal attribution questions out of scope. P002 (optical lattice clock) is a clean, mature two-name invention but narrower in reach and with a closer overlap to the 2005 and 2012 prizes; a prize is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; documented ties to Chalmers colleagues and the 2025 laureates' circuit field are not connected to the P001 or P002 laureates
